hero.eyebrow: The Nick Virgilio Haiku Association & Writers House
hero.headline: Where Camden and the world write, reflect and gather.
hero.text: The Nick Virgilio Haiku Association & Writers House brings twenty years of readings, workshops, publications and youth outreach to Waterfront South, Camden — all honoring the poetry of American haikuist Nicholas Virgilio.

featured.title: Student Haiku And Senryu Anthology 2022-2026
featured.text:
In this first edition of the Nick Virgilio Writers House Youth Anthology, we collect the winners, and for the first time, the finalists of the Nick Virgilio Memorial Student Haiku and Senryu Competition from the years 2022-2026.

This book brings together the best middle and high school poets from around the country and around the world, from Georgia to California, and from Romania to Samoa. These students prove that poetry is humanity defined, and that haiku in particular reveals what it means to be human.

actions.blurb: Readings, open mics and the monthly Midnight Notes in Waterfront South.
actions.title: Life at the Writers House
actions.text: The Virgilio Writers House in Waterfront South, Camden hosts readings, open mics, ginko walks and the monthly Midnight Notes series. Stop by for an event, visit by appointment, or book the space for your own gathering.

actions.blurb: A weekly prompt, recorded workshops and a youth contest for short-form poets everywhere.
actions.title: For poets & haikuists
actions.text: Join a worldwide community of short-form poets. Answer the weekly Haiku in Action prompt, learn the form in our recorded workshops, and encourage young writers through our annual youth contest.

actions.blurb: The Tiny Truth Project brings mindful short-form writing into Camden classrooms.
actions.title: For teachers & schools
actions.text: The Tiny Truth Project brings mindfulness and literacy into the classroom through short-form creative writing. Now in its third year, it has reached 123 students across three Camden schools, with teachers trained to keep it going.
